# One-sided two-sample t-test power calculation
# Independent groups, equal variances, 1:1 allocation
# Effect size (difference): 4.3 dBA
# Common SD: 7.8 dBA
# Target power: 0.8
# Significance level: 0.05 (one-sided)

library(stats)

# Parameters
delta <- 4.3  # difference in means
sigma <- 7.8  # common standard deviation
alpha <- 0.05  # significance level (one-sided)
target_power <- 0.8
allocation_ratio <- 1

# For a one-sided t-test with equal variances and equal sample sizes (n per group):
# The noncentrality parameter is:
# lambda = (delta / sigma) * sqrt(n / 2)
# where n is the per-group sample size

# We need to find the critical value t_alpha for the one-sided test
# and then find n such that power = P(T > t_alpha | H1) >= 0.8

# Degrees of freedom: df = 2n - 2
# Critical value for one-sided test at alpha = 0.05
t_alpha <- qt(1 - alpha, df = Inf)  # using normal approximation initially
print(paste("Critical value (normal approximation):", round(t_alpha, 4)))

# Standardized effect size (Cohen's d)
cohens_d <- delta / sigma
print(paste("Cohen's d:", round(cohens_d, 4)))

# For power calculation, we use the noncentrality parameter
# Using the power.t.test function from base R
result <- power.t.test(
  n = NULL,  # find sample size
  delta = delta,
  sd = sigma,
  sig.level = alpha,
  power = target_power,
  type = "two.sample",
  alternative = "one.sided"
)

print(result)

n_continuous <- result$n
n_per_group <- ceiling(n_continuous)

print(paste("\nContinuous solution (n per group):", round(n_continuous, 4)))
print(paste("Rounded up to integer (n per group):", n_per_group))

# Verify the power at this sample size
power_at_n <- power.t.test(
  n = n_per_group,
  delta = delta,
  sd = sigma,
  sig.level = alpha,
  power = NULL,
  type = "two.sample",
  alternative = "one.sided"
)

print(paste("\nAchieved power at n =", n_per_group, ":", round(power_at_n$power, 6)))

# Check power at n-1 to show this is indeed the minimum
if (n_per_group > 1) {
  power_at_n_minus_1 <- power.t.test(
    n = n_per_group - 1,
    delta = delta,
    sd = sigma,
    sig.level = alpha,
    power = NULL,
    type = "two.sample",
    alternative = "one.sided"
  )
  print(paste("Power at n =", n_per_group - 1, ":", round(power_at_n_minus_1$power, 6)))
}

# Prepare results
results_json <- list(
  results = list(
    list(
      metric = "sample_size",
      value = n_per_group,
      unit = "participants_per_group"
    ),
    list(
      metric = "achieved_power",
      value = round(power_at_n$power, 6),
      unit = "probability"
    ),
    list(
      metric = "continuous_solution",
      value = round(n_continuous, 4),
      unit = "participants_per_group"
    ),
    list(
      metric = "power_at_n_minus_1",
      value = round(power_at_n_minus_1$power, 6),
      unit = "probability"
    )
  )
)

cat("POWER_AGENT_RESULT=", jsonlite::toJSON(results_json, auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15), "\n")
